manualTranslations.zh: 謐性暴虐，明帝初，台使元延到其州界，以驛邏無兵，攝帥檢核。
manualTranslations.literal: Mi was violent and cruel by nature. At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign, the court envoy Yuan Yan reached the borders of his province and, because the postal patrol had no soldiers, detained the commander for investigation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mi was violent and cruel by nature. At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign, the court envoy Yuan Yan reached the borders of his province and, because the postal patrol had no soldiers, detained the commander for investigation.

manualTranslations.zh: 隊主高保願列言：「所有之兵，王皆私役。」
manualTranslations.literal: Unit leader Gao Baoyuan stated in a report, "All the soldiers there are being used privately by the prince."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Unit leader Gao Baoyuan stated in a report, "All the soldiers there are being used privately by the prince."

manualTranslations.zh: 謐聞，大怒，鞭保願等五人各二百。
manualTranslations.literal: When Mi heard of this, he was furious and flogged Baoyuan and four others two hundred strokes each.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Mi heard of this, he was furious and flogged Baoyuan and four others two hundred strokes each.

manualTranslations.zh: 數日間，謐召近州人夫，閉四門，內外嚴固，搜掩城人，楚掠備至。
manualTranslations.literal: Within a few days, Mi summoned laborers from nearby provinces, closed the four gates, tightened the defenses within and without, searched and seized people in the city, and subjected them to every kind of beating and torture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Within a few days, Mi summoned laborers from nearby provinces, closed the four gates, tightened the defenses within and without, searched and seized people in the city, and subjected them to every kind of beating and torture.

manualTranslations.zh: 又無事而斬六人，合城兇懼。
manualTranslations.literal: He also beheaded six people without cause, and the whole city was terrified.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also beheaded six people without cause, and the whole city was terrified.

manualTranslations.zh: 眾遂大呼，屯門。
manualTranslations.literal: The crowd then cried out loudly and gathered at the gates.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The crowd then cried out loudly and gathered at the gates.

manualTranslations.zh: 謐怖，登樓毀梯以自固。
manualTranslations.literal: Mi was frightened, climbed a tower, and destroyed the ladder to secure himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mi was frightened, climbed a tower, and destroyed the ladder to secure himself.

manualTranslations.zh: 士人散走，城人分守四門。
manualTranslations.literal: The gentlemen scattered and fled, while the city people divided up and guarded the four gates.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The gentlemen scattered and fled, while the city people divided up and guarded the four gates.

manualTranslations.zh: 靈太后遣遊擊將軍王竫馳驛喻之。
manualTranslations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling sent Mobile General Wang Jing by courier relay to instruct them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling sent Mobile General Wang Jing by courier relay to instruct them.

manualTranslations.zh: 城人既見靖至，開門謝罪。
manualTranslations.literal: When the city people saw Jing arrive, they opened the gates and apologized for their offense.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the city people saw Jing arrive, they opened the gates and apologized for their offense.

manualTranslations.zh: 乃罷謐州，除大司農卿。
manualTranslations.literal: Mi was then removed from his provincial post and appointed Chamberlain for the National Treasury.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mi was then removed from his provincial post and appointed Chamberlain for the National Treasury.

manualTranslations.zh: 遷幽州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: He was transferred to be governor of Youzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was transferred to be governor of Youzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 謐妃胡氏，靈太后從女也。
manualTranslations.literal: Mi's consort, Lady Hu, was Empress Dowager Ling's niece.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mi's consort, Lady Hu, was Empress Dowager Ling's niece.

manualTranslations.zh: 未發，坐毆其妃，免官。
manualTranslations.literal: Before he departed, he was dismissed from office for beating his consort.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Before he departed, he was dismissed from office for beating his consort.

manualTranslations.zh: 後除都官尚書。
manualTranslations.literal: Later he was appointed Minister of Justice.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Minister of Justice.

manualTranslations.zh: 車駕出拜圓丘，謐與妃乘赤馬犯鹵簿，為御史所彈，靈太后特不問。
manualTranslations.literal: When the imperial carriage went out to worship at the Round Mound, Mi and his consort rode red horses and violated the imperial procession. They were impeached by the censor, but Empress Dowager Ling specifically declined to inquire into it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage went out to worship at the Round Mound, Mi and his consort rode red horses and violated the imperial procession. They were impeached by the censor, but Empress Dowager Ling specifically declined to inquire into it.

manualTranslations.zh: 薨，高陽王雍，幹之母弟，啟論謐，贈假侍中、司州牧，諡貞景。
manualTranslations.literal: When he died, Yong, Prince of Gaoyang, Gan's younger brother by the same mother, submitted a petition discussing Mi, and Mi was posthumously granted Acting Palace Attendant and Governor of Sizhou, with the posthumous name Zhenjing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he died, Yong, Prince of Gaoyang, Gan's younger brother by the same mother, submitted a petition discussing Mi, and Mi was posthumously granted Acting Palace Attendant and Governor of Sizhou, with the posthumous name Zhenjing.

sourceRange.text: 有司奏：「廣川王妃薨于代京，未審以新尊從於卑舊，為宜卑舊來就新尊？」詔曰：「遷洛之人，自茲厥後，悉可歸骸芒嶺，皆不得就塋恆、代。其有夫先葬北，婦今喪在南，婦人從夫，宜還代葬。若欲移父就母，亦得任之。其有妻墳于恆、代，夫死於洛，不得以尊就卑。欲移母就父，宜亦從之。若異葬，亦從之。若不在葬限，身在代喪，葬之彼此，皆得任之。其戶屬恆、燕，身官京洛，去留之宜，亦從所擇。其屬諸州諸，各得任意。」詔贈諧武衛將軍，諡曰剛。及葬，帝親臨送之。子靈道襲。卒，諡悼王。齊郡王簡字叔亮，太和五年封，位中都大官。簡母，沮渠牧犍女也。簡性貌特類外祖。後為內都大官。孝文嘗與簡俱朝文明太后皇信堂，簡居帝之右，行家人禮。遷太保。孝文仁孝，以諸父零落，存者唯簡，每見，立以待之；俟坐，致敬問起居，停簡拜伏。簡性好酒，不能理公私之事。妻常氏，燕郡公喜女也，文明太后以賜簡。幹綜家事，頗節簡酒。乃至盜竊，求乞婢侍，卒不能禁。薨時，孝文不豫，詔曰：「叔父薨背，痛慕摧絕，不自勝任。但虛頓床枕，未堪奉赴，當力疾發哀。」諡曰靈王。宣武時，改諡曰順。子祐，字伯授。母常氏，孝文以納不以禮，不許其為妃。宣武以母從子貴，詔特拜為齊國太妃。祐位涇州刺史。薨，諡曰敬。河間王若字叔儒，未封而薨。追封河間，諡曰孝。詔京兆康王子太安為後。太安于若為從弟，非相後之義，廢之。以齊郡王子琛繼。

context.beforeSource: 」諧將大斂，帝素委貌深衣哭之，入室哀慟，撫屍而出。
context.afterSource: 琛字曇寶，幼敏慧，孝文愛之。

manualTranslations.zh: 有司奏：「廣川王妃薨于代京，未審以新尊從於卑舊，為宜卑舊來就新尊？」
manualTranslations.literal: The responsible offices memorialized, "The consort of the Prince of Guangchuan has died in the Dai capital. We are unsure whether the newly honored should follow the old and humble, or whether the old and humble should come to join the newly honored?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The responsible offices memorialized, "The consort of the Prince of Guangchuan has died in the Dai capital. We are unsure whether the newly honored should follow the old and humble, or whether the old and humble should come to join the newly honored?"

manualTranslations.zh: 詔曰：「遷洛之人，自茲厥後，悉可歸骸芒嶺，皆不得就塋恆、代。
manualTranslations.literal: An edict said, "Those who moved to Luoyang, from now on, may all return their remains to Mangling, and none may go to the graveyards at Heng and Dai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Those who moved to Luoyang, from now on, may all return their remains to Mangling, and none may go to the graveyards at Heng and Dai.

manualTranslations.zh: 其有夫先葬北，婦今喪在南，婦人從夫，宜還代葬。
manualTranslations.literal: If a husband was previously buried in the north and his wife now dies in the south, since a woman follows her husband, she should be returned to Dai for burial.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If a husband was previously buried in the north and his wife now dies in the south, since a woman follows her husband, she should be returned to Dai for burial.

manualTranslations.zh: 若欲移父就母，亦得任之。
manualTranslations.literal: If they wish to move the father to join the mother, this too may be permitted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If they wish to move the father to join the mother, this too may be permitted.

manualTranslations.zh: 其有妻墳于恆、代，夫死於洛，不得以尊就卑。
manualTranslations.literal: If a wife has a tomb in Heng or Dai and the husband dies in Luoyang, the honored may not go to the humble.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If a wife has a tomb in Heng or Dai and the husband dies in Luoyang, the honored may not go to the humble.

manualTranslations.zh: 欲移母就父，宜亦從之。
manualTranslations.literal: If they wish to move the mother to join the father, this too should be permitted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If they wish to move the mother to join the father, this too should be permitted.

manualTranslations.zh: 若異葬，亦從之。
manualTranslations.literal: If they choose separate burials, this too is allowed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If they choose separate burials, this too is allowed.

manualTranslations.zh: 若不在葬限，身在代喪，葬之彼此，皆得任之。
manualTranslations.literal: If the case does not fall within the burial rules and the person dies while in Dai, burial there or here may both be left to their choice.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If the case does not fall within the burial rules and the person dies while in Dai, burial there or here may both be left to their choice.

manualTranslations.zh: 其戶屬恆、燕，身官京洛，去留之宜，亦從所擇。
manualTranslations.literal: If the household belongs to Heng or Yan but the person holds office in the capital Luoyang, whether to remain or go should also follow what they choose.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If the household belongs to Heng or Yan but the person holds office in the capital Luoyang, whether to remain or go should also follow what they choose.

manualTranslations.zh: 其屬諸州諸，各得任意。」
manualTranslations.literal: Those who belong to the various provinces may each do as they wish."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those who belong to the various provinces may each do as they wish."

manualTranslations.zh: 詔贈諧武衛將軍，諡曰剛。
manualTranslations.literal: An edict posthumously granted Xie the title General of the Martial Guard and gave him the posthumous name Gang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously granted Xie the title General of the Martial Guard and gave him the posthumous name Gang.

manualTranslations.zh: 及葬，帝親臨送之。
manualTranslations.literal: When he was buried, the emperor personally attended and escorted him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he was buried, the emperor personally attended and escorted him.

manualTranslations.zh: 子靈道襲。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Lingdao inherited the title.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Lingdao inherited the title.

manualTranslations.zh: 卒，諡悼王。
manualTranslations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously named Prince Dao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously named Prince Dao.

manualTranslations.zh: 齊郡王簡字叔亮，太和五年封，位中都大官。
manualTranslations.literal: Jian, Prince of Qi Commandery, was styled Shuliang. He was enfeoffed in the fifth year of Taihe and held office as Chief Official of the Central Capital.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jian, Prince of Qi Commandery, was styled Shuliang. He was enfeoffed in the fifth year of Taihe and held office as Chief Official of the Central Capital.

manualTranslations.zh: 簡母，沮渠牧犍女也。
manualTranslations.literal: Jian's mother was a daughter of Juqu Mujian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jian's mother was a daughter of Juqu Mujian.

manualTranslations.zh: 簡性貌特類外祖。
manualTranslations.literal: In nature and appearance, Jian especially resembled his maternal grandfather.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In nature and appearance, Jian especially resembled his maternal grandfather.

manualTranslations.zh: 後為內都大官。
manualTranslations.literal: Later he became Chief Official of the Inner Capital.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later he became Chief Official of the Inner Capital.

manualTranslations.zh: 孝文嘗與簡俱朝文明太后皇信堂，簡居帝之右，行家人禮。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen once attended on Empress Dowager Wenming with Jian in the Huangxin Hall; Jian sat to the emperor's right, and they observed the rites of family members.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen once attended on Empress Dowager Wenming with Jian in the Huangxin Hall; Jian sat to the emperor's right, and they observed the rites of family members.

manualTranslations.zh: 遷太保。
manualTranslations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Protector.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Protector.

manualTranslations.zh: 孝文仁孝，以諸父零落，存者唯簡，每見，立以待之；
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen was benevolent and filial; because his uncles had withered away and only Jian survived, whenever he saw Jian, he stood to wait for him;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen was benevolent and filial; because his uncles had withered away and only Jian survived, whenever he saw Jian, he stood to wait for him;

manualTranslations.zh: 俟坐，致敬問起居，停簡拜伏。
manualTranslations.literal: when Jian was seated, the emperor respectfully asked after his health and stopped Jian from bowing prostrate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: when Jian was seated, the emperor respectfully asked after his health and stopped Jian from bowing prostrate.

manualTranslations.zh: 簡性好酒，不能理公私之事。
manualTranslations.literal: Jian loved wine by nature and could not manage public or private affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jian loved wine by nature and could not manage public or private affairs.

manualTranslations.zh: 妻常氏，燕郡公喜女也，文明太后以賜簡。
manualTranslations.literal: His wife, Lady Chang, was a daughter of Xi, Duke of Yan Commandery, and Empress Dowager Wenming bestowed her on Jian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Chang, was a daughter of Xi, Duke of Yan Commandery, and Empress Dowager Wenming bestowed her on Jian.

manualTranslations.zh: 幹綜家事，頗節簡酒。
manualTranslations.literal: She managed the household affairs and somewhat limited Jian's drinking.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She managed the household affairs and somewhat limited Jian's drinking.

manualTranslations.zh: 乃至盜竊，求乞婢侍，卒不能禁。
manualTranslations.literal: He even stole and begged from maidservants, and in the end she could not restrain him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He even stole and begged from maidservants, and in the end she could not restrain him.

manualTranslations.zh: 薨時，孝文不豫，詔曰：「叔父薨背，痛慕摧絕，不自勝任。
manualTranslations.literal: When he died, Emperor Xiaowen was ill. The edict said, "My uncle has died and departed; my grief and longing are crushing, beyond what I can bear.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he died, Emperor Xiaowen was ill. The edict said, "My uncle has died and departed; my grief and longing are crushing, beyond what I can bear.

manualTranslations.zh: 但虛頓床枕，未堪奉赴，當力疾發哀。」
manualTranslations.literal: But I am weak and prostrate on bed and pillow and cannot yet go in attendance. I shall force myself through illness to send forth mourning."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: But I am weak and prostrate on bed and pillow and cannot yet go in attendance. I shall force myself through illness to send forth mourning."

manualTranslations.zh: 諡曰靈王。
manualTranslations.literal: He was posthumously named Prince Ling.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named Prince Ling.

manualTranslations.zh: 宣武時，改諡曰順。
manualTranslations.literal: In Xuanwu's time, the posthumous name was changed to Shun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Xuanwu's time, the posthumous name was changed to Shun.

manualTranslations.zh: 子祐，字伯授。
manualTranslations.literal: His son You was styled Boshu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son You was styled Boshu.

manualTranslations.zh: 母常氏，孝文以納不以禮，不許其為妃。
manualTranslations.literal: His mother was Lady Chang; because Emperor Xiaowen considered that she had not been received according to ritual, he did not permit her to be made consort.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His mother was Lady Chang; because Emperor Xiaowen considered that she had not been received according to ritual, he did not permit her to be made consort.

manualTranslations.zh: 宣武以母從子貴，詔特拜為齊國太妃。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu, on the principle that a mother is honored by her son, issued an edict specially appointing her Grand Consort of the Qi State.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu, on the principle that a mother is honored by her son, issued an edict specially appointing her Grand Consort of the Qi State.

manualTranslations.zh: 祐位涇州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: You held the post of governor of Jingzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You held the post of governor of Jingzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 薨，諡曰敬。
manualTranslations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously named Jing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously named Jing.

manualTranslations.zh: 河間王若字叔儒，未封而薨。
manualTranslations.literal: Ruo, Prince of Hejian, was styled Shuru and died before being enfeoffed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ruo, Prince of Hejian, was styled Shuru and died before being enfeoffed.

manualTranslations.zh: 追封河間，諡曰孝。
manualTranslations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Hejian and given the posthumous name Xiao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Hejian and given the posthumous name Xiao.

manualTranslations.zh: 詔京兆康王子太安為後。
manualTranslations.literal: An edict made Tai'an, son of Prince Kang of Jingzhao, his heir.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An edict made Tai'an, son of Prince Kang of Jingzhao, his heir.

manualTranslations.zh: 太安于若為從弟，非相後之義，廢之。
manualTranslations.literal: Tai'an was Ruo's younger cousin, which was not proper for succession, so he was removed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tai'an was Ruo's younger cousin, which was not proper for succession, so he was removed.

manualTranslations.zh: 以齊郡王子琛繼。
manualTranslations.literal: Chen, son of the Prince of Qi Commandery, was made successor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chen, son of the Prince of Qi Commandery, was made successor.

sourceRange.text: 太武即位，拜駕部尚書。車駕征蠕蠕大檀，分為五道。遷尚書左僕射，進爵河間公。原在朝無所比周，然恃寵驕恣，多所排抑。為子求襄城公盧魯元女，魯元不許。原告其罪狀，事相連逮，歷時不決。原懼不勝，遂謀逆，事泄，伏誅。原兄弟外節儉而內實積聚，及誅後，籍其財至數萬。

context.beforeSource: 蠕蠕犯塞，原輒破之，以功賜爵武原侯，加魯兵將軍。
context.afterSource: 弟頡，辯慧多策略，最有父風。

manualTranslations.zh: 太武即位，拜駕部尚書。
manualTranslations.literal: When Taiwu ascended the throne, Yuan was appointed Minister of the Carriage Bureau.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Taiwu ascended the throne, Yuan was appointed Minister of the Carriage Bureau.

manualTranslations.zh: 車駕征蠕蠕大檀，分為五道。
manualTranslations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned against the Rouran ruler Datan, the army was divided into five routes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage campaigned against the Rouran ruler Datan, the army was divided into five routes.

manualTranslations.zh: 遷尚書左僕射，進爵河間公。
manualTranslations.literal: He was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and advanced in title to Duke of Hejian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and advanced in title to Duke of Hejian.

manualTranslations.zh: 原在朝無所比周，然恃寵驕恣，多所排抑。
manualTranslations.literal: At court, Yuan formed no cliques, but relying on favor he became arrogant and willful and suppressed many people.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At court, Yuan formed no cliques, but relying on favor he became arrogant and willful and suppressed many people.

manualTranslations.zh: 為子求襄城公盧魯元女，魯元不許。
manualTranslations.literal: He sought a daughter of Lu Luyuan, Duke of Xiangcheng, for his son, but Luyuan would not agree.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He sought a daughter of Lu Luyuan, Duke of Xiangcheng, for his son, but Luyuan would not agree.

manualTranslations.zh: 原告其罪狀，事相連逮，歷時不決。
manualTranslations.literal: Yuan accused him of crimes; the affair implicated others in succession and remained unresolved for a long time.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan accused him of crimes; the affair implicated others in succession and remained unresolved for a long time.

manualTranslations.zh: 原懼不勝，遂謀逆，事泄，伏誅。
manualTranslations.literal: Yuan feared he could not prevail and so plotted rebellion. When the affair leaked, he was executed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan feared he could not prevail and so plotted rebellion. When the affair leaked, he was executed.

manualTranslations.zh: 原兄弟外節儉而內實積聚，及誅後，籍其財至數萬。
manualTranslations.literal: Yuan and his brothers seemed frugal outwardly, but in private they had amassed wealth; after their execution, the inventory of their property reached tens of thousands.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan and his brothers seemed frugal outwardly, but in private they had amassed wealth; after their execution, the inventory of their property reached tens of thousands.

sourceRange.text: 婁伏連，代人也。代為酋帥。伏連忠厚有器量，年十三，襲父位，領部落。道武初，從破賀蘭部，又平中山。及征姚平于柴壁，以功賜爵安邑侯。明元時，為晉兵將軍、并州刺史。太武即位，封廣陵公，再遷光祿勳，進爵為王。後鎮統萬。薨，諡恭王。

context.beforeSource: 卒，子伊利襲。
context.afterSource: 子真襲，降爵為公。

context.afterLocal: 子真襲，降爵為公。

manualTranslations.zh: 婁伏連，代人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Lou Fulian was a man of Dai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lou Fulian was a man of Dai.

manualTranslations.zh: 代為酋帥。
manualTranslations.literal: For generations his family had been tribal chiefs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For generations his family had been tribal chiefs.

manualTranslations.zh: 伏連忠厚有器量，年十三，襲父位，領部落。
manualTranslations.literal: Fulian was loyal, generous, and capable; at thirteen he inherited his father's position and led the tribe.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fulian was loyal, generous, and capable; at thirteen he inherited his father's position and led the tribe.

manualTranslations.zh: 道武初，從破賀蘭部，又平中山。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of Daowu's reign, he followed in breaking the Helan tribe and also pacified Zhongshan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daowu's reign, he followed in breaking the Helan tribe and also pacified Zhongshan.

manualTranslations.zh: 及征姚平于柴壁，以功賜爵安邑侯。
manualTranslations.literal: When Yao Ping was campaigned against at Chaibi, Fulian received the title Marquis of Anyi for his merit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Yao Ping was campaigned against at Chaibi, Fulian received the title Marquis of Anyi for his merit.

manualTranslations.zh: 明元時，為晉兵將軍、并州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: In Mingyuan's time, he served as General of Jin Troops and governor of Bingzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Mingyuan's time, he served as General of Jin Troops and governor of Bingzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 太武即位，封廣陵公，再遷光祿勳，進爵為王。
manualTranslations.literal: When Taiwu ascended the throne, Fulian was enfeoffed as Duke of Guangling, twice promoted to Director of the Imperial Household, and advanced in title to prince.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Taiwu ascended the throne, Fulian was enfeoffed as Duke of Guangling, twice promoted to Director of the Imperial Household, and advanced in title to prince.

manualTranslations.zh: 後鎮統萬。
manualTranslations.literal: Later he garrisoned Tongwan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later he garrisoned Tongwan.

manualTranslations.zh: 薨，諡恭王。
manualTranslations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously named Prince Gong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously named Prince Gong.

sourceRange.text: 諾長子眷，忠謹有父風。明元時，執事左右，為太官令。時侍臣受斤亡入蠕蠕，詔眷追之。遂至虜庭，禽之大檀前。由是以驍烈聞。太武即位，命眷與散騎侍郎劉庫仁等八人分典四部，綰奏機要，加陳兵將軍。文成時，拜侍中、太尉，封漁陽王，與太宰常英等錄尚書事。文成北巡狩，以寒雪方降，議還。眷曰：「今去都不遠而旋，虜必疑我有內難。方寒雪，宜更進前。」帝遂度漠而還。帝以眷元老，賜杖履上殿。薨，諡曰莊。子多侯襲爵。

manualTranslations.literal: Nuo's eldest son Juan was loyal and careful and had his father's manner.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Nuo's eldest son Juan was loyal and careful and had his father's manner.

manualTranslations.zh: 明元時，執事左右，為太官令。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that time the attendant Shoujin fled to the Rouran, and an edict ordered Juan to pursue him.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: He went all the way to the enemy court and captured Shoujin before Datan.

manualTranslations.zh: 由是以驍烈聞。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: From this he became known for fierce bravery.

manualTranslations.zh: 太武即位，命眷與散騎侍郎劉庫仁等八人分典四部，綰奏機要，加陳兵將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: When Taiwu ascended the throne, he ordered Juan, Cavalier Attendant Liu Kuren, and eight others to divide charge of the four departments and manage key memorials, and he added the title General Who Deploys Troops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Taiwu ascended the throne, he ordered Juan, Cavalier Attendant Liu Kuren, and eight others to divide charge of the four departments and manage key memorials, and he added the title General Who Deploys Troops.

manualTranslations.zh: 文成時，拜侍中、太尉，封漁陽王，與太宰常英等錄尚書事。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Wencheng's time, Juan was appointed Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant, enfeoffed as Prince of Yuyang, and, together with Grand Steward Chang Ying and others, recorded the affairs of the Masters of Writing.

manualTranslations.zh: 文成北巡狩，以寒雪方降，議還。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Wencheng made a northern inspection tour, cold snow had just begun to fall and the court discussed returning.

manualTranslations.zh: 眷曰：「今去都不遠而旋，虜必疑我有內難。
manualTranslations.literal: Juan said, "If we turn back now while not far from the capital, the enemy will surely suspect we have internal trouble.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Juan said, "If we turn back now while not far from the capital, the enemy will surely suspect we have internal trouble.

manualTranslations.zh: 方寒雪，宜更進前。」
manualTranslations.literal: Since it is cold and snowing, we should advance farther."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since it is cold and snowing, we should advance farther."

manualTranslations.zh: 帝遂度漠而還。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor then crossed the desert and returned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor then crossed the desert and returned.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝以眷元老，賜杖履上殿。
manualTranslations.literal: Because Juan was an elder statesman, the emperor permitted him to ascend the hall with staff and shoes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because Juan was an elder statesman, the emperor permitted him to ascend the hall with staff and shoes.

manualTranslations.zh: 薨，諡曰莊。
manualTranslations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously named Zhuang.

manualTranslations.zh: 子多侯襲爵。

sourceRange.text: 道武為魏王，崇從平中原，位侍中、豫州刺史、太尉、宜都公。天賜三年，薨。先是，衛王儀謀逆，崇預焉。道武惜其功，秘之。及有司奏諡，帝親覽諡法，述義不克曰丁，曰：「此當矣。」乃諡丁公。

sourceRange.text: 長子俊，字醜歸，少聰敏。年十五，內侍左右，性謹密，初無過行。以便弓馬，轉為獵郎。道武崩，清河王紹閉宮門，明元在外。紹拘逼俊以為己援。外雖從紹，內實忠款，仍與元磨渾等說紹歸明元。時明元左右唯車路頭、王洛兒等，及得俊等，大悅，以為爪牙。及即位，稍遷衛將軍，賜爵安成公。及硃提王悅懷刃入禁，欲行大逆。俊覺悅舉動有異，乃於悅懷中得兩刃匕首，遂執悅殺之。明元以俊前後功重，軍國大計一以委之。群官上事，先由俊銓校，然後奏聞。性平正柔和，未嘗有喜怒色。忠篤愛厚，不諂上抑下。每奉詔宣外，必告示殷勤。是以上下嘉歎。泰常元年，卒，時年二十八。明元親臨哀慟，朝野無不追惜。贈司空、安成王，諡孝元，賜溫明秘器，載以巉輬車，衛士導從，陪葬金陵。子蒲襲爵。後有大功及寵倖貴臣薨，賵賻送終禮皆依俊故事，無得逾之者。

manualTranslations.zh: 長子俊，字醜歸，少聰敏。
manualTranslations.literal: The eldest son Jun was styled Chougui and was intelligent and perceptive from youth.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The eldest son Jun was styled Chougui and was intelligent and perceptive from youth.

manualTranslations.zh: 年十五，內侍左右，性謹密，初無過行。
manualTranslations.literal: At fifteen, he served inside at the ruler's side; by nature he was careful and discreet, and at first he committed no misconduct.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At fifteen, he served inside at the ruler's side; by nature he was careful and discreet, and at first he committed no misconduct.

manualTranslations.zh: 以便弓馬，轉為獵郎。
manualTranslations.literal: Because he was skilled with bow and horse, he was transferred to be a Hunting Gentleman.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because he was skilled with bow and horse, he was transferred to be a Hunting Gentleman.

manualTranslations.zh: 道武崩，清河王紹閉宮門，明元在外。
manualTranslations.literal: When Daowu died, Prince Shao of Qinghe closed the palace gates while Mingyuan was outside.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Daowu died, Prince Shao of Qinghe closed the palace gates while Mingyuan was outside.

manualTranslations.zh: 紹拘逼俊以為己援。
manualTranslations.literal: Shao detained and coerced Jun, making him his support.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shao detained and coerced Jun, making him his support.

manualTranslations.zh: 外雖從紹，內實忠款，仍與元磨渾等說紹歸明元。
manualTranslations.literal: Although outwardly Jun followed Shao, inwardly he was loyal and sincere, and with Yuan Mohun and others he persuaded Shao to submit to Mingyuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Although outwardly Jun followed Shao, inwardly he was loyal and sincere, and with Yuan Mohun and others he persuaded Shao to submit to Mingyuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 時明元左右唯車路頭、王洛兒等，及得俊等，大悅，以為爪牙。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time only Che Lutou, Wang Luo'er, and a few others were at Mingyuan's side; when he obtained Jun and the others, he was greatly pleased and made them his trusted claws and teeth.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that time only Che Lutou, Wang Luo'er, and a few others were at Mingyuan's side; when he obtained Jun and the others, he was greatly pleased and made them his trusted claws and teeth.

manualTranslations.zh: 及即位，稍遷衛將軍，賜爵安成公。
manualTranslations.literal: After Mingyuan ascended the throne, Jun was gradually promoted to General of the Guards and given the title Duke of Ancheng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Mingyuan ascended the throne, Jun was gradually promoted to General of the Guards and given the title Duke of Ancheng.

manualTranslations.zh: 及硃提王悅懷刃入禁，欲行大逆。
manualTranslations.literal: When Yue, Prince of Zhuti, entered the forbidden precincts carrying blades and intended to commit great treason,
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Yue, Prince of Zhuti, entered the forbidden precincts carrying blades and intended to commit great treason,

manualTranslations.zh: 俊覺悅舉動有異，乃於悅懷中得兩刃匕首，遂執悅殺之。
manualTranslations.literal: Jun noticed that Yue's movements were unusual, found two double-edged daggers in his clothing, and seized and killed him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jun noticed that Yue's movements were unusual, found two double-edged daggers in his clothing, and seized and killed him.

manualTranslations.zh: 明元以俊前後功重，軍國大計一以委之。
manualTranslations.literal: Because Jun's earlier and later merits were weighty, Mingyuan entrusted all major military and state plans to him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because Jun's earlier and later merits were weighty, Mingyuan entrusted all major military and state plans to him.

manualTranslations.zh: 群官上事，先由俊銓校，然後奏聞。
manualTranslations.literal: When the officials submitted matters, they first passed through Jun for weighing and review, and only afterward were memorialized to the throne.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the officials submitted matters, they first passed through Jun for weighing and review, and only afterward were memorialized to the throne.

manualTranslations.zh: 性平正柔和，未嘗有喜怒色。
manualTranslations.literal: His nature was fair, upright, gentle, and harmonious, and he never showed joy or anger on his face.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His nature was fair, upright, gentle, and harmonious, and he never showed joy or anger on his face.

manualTranslations.zh: 忠篤愛厚，不諂上抑下。
manualTranslations.literal: He was loyal, sincere, loving, and generous, and did not flatter those above or oppress those below.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was loyal, sincere, loving, and generous, and did not flatter those above or oppress those below.

manualTranslations.zh: 每奉詔宣外，必告示殷勤。
manualTranslations.literal: Whenever he received an edict to announce outside the palace, he always explained it with earnest care.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Whenever he received an edict to announce outside the palace, he always explained it with earnest care.

manualTranslations.zh: 是以上下嘉歎。
manualTranslations.literal: For this, high and low praised and admired him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For this, high and low praised and admired him.

manualTranslations.zh: 泰常元年，卒，時年二十八。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Taichang, he died at the age of twenty-eight.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taichang, he died at the age of twenty-eight.

manualTranslations.zh: 明元親臨哀慟，朝野無不追惜。
manualTranslations.literal: Mingyuan personally came and mourned bitterly, and court and countryside alike grieved for him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mingyuan personally came and mourned bitterly, and court and countryside alike grieved for him.

manualTranslations.zh: 贈司空、安成王，諡孝元，賜溫明秘器，載以巉輬車，衛士導從，陪葬金陵。
manualTranslations.literal: He was posthumously granted Minister of Works and Prince of Ancheng, given the posthumous name Xiaoyuan, presented with an imperial coffin, carried in a chanliang funeral carriage, escorted by guards, and buried in attendance at Jinling.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Minister of Works and Prince of Ancheng, given the posthumous name Xiaoyuan, presented with an imperial coffin, carried in a chanliang funeral carriage, escorted by guards, and buried in attendance at Jinling.

manualTranslations.zh: 子蒲襲爵。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Pu inherited the title.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Pu inherited the title.

manualTranslations.zh: 後有大功及寵倖貴臣薨，賵賻送終禮皆依俊故事，無得逾之者。
manualTranslations.literal: Later, whenever ministers of great merit or favored noble status died, the gifts, funeral assistance, and rites for sending them off all followed Jun's precedent, and none was permitted to exceed it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later, whenever ministers of great merit or favored noble status died, the gifts, funeral assistance, and rites for sending them off all followed Jun's precedent, and none was permitted to exceed it.

sourceRange.text: 明元即位，命同與南平公長孫嵩並理人訟。又詔同與肥如侯賀護持節循察並、定二州及諸山居雜胡、丁零。宣詔撫慰，問其疾苦，糾舉守宰不法，郡國肅然。同東出井陘。至钜鹿，發眾欲修大嶺山，通天門關。又築城于宋子，以鎮靜郡縣。護嫉同得眾心，使人告同築城聚眾，欲圖大事。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Mingyuan ascended the throne, he ordered Tong and Zhangsun Song, Duke of Nanping, to jointly handle the people's lawsuits.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also ordered Tong and He Hu, Marquis of Feiru, to hold tallies and inspect Bingzhou, Dingzhou, and the mixed Hu and Dingling living in the mountains.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tong went east through Jingxing.

sourceRange.text: 桓帝崩後，操立碑於大邗城南，以頌功德，云「魏，軒轅之苗裔」。言桓、穆二帝「統國禦眾，威禁大行，國無奸盜，路有頌聲。威武所向，下無交兵。招喻六狄，咸來歸誠。奉承晉皇，扞禦邊疆。王室多難，天網弛綱。豪心遠濟，靡離其殃。歲翦逆命，奸盜豺狼。永安元年，歲次甲子。奸黨猶逆，東西狼歭。敢逼天王，兵甲屢起。怙眾肆暴，虐用將士。鄴、洛構隙，棄親求疏。乃招異類，屠各、匈奴。交刃千里，長蛇塞塗。晉道應天，言展良謨。使持節、平北將軍、并州刺史、護匈奴中郎將、東嬴公司馬騰，才神絕世，規略超遠。欲求外救，朝臣莫應。簡賢選士，命茲良使。遣參軍壺倫、牙門中行嘉、義陽亭侯衛謨、協義亭侯衛鹁健等，馳奉檄書，至晉陽城」。又稱桓、穆二帝，「心存宸極。輔相二衛，對揚毗翼。操展文謀，雄奮武烈。承命會議，諮論奮發。翼衛內外，鎮靜四方。忠恕用暉，外動亦攘。功濟方州，勳烈光延。升平之日，納貢充籓。馮瞻鑾蓋，步趾三川。有德無祿，大命不延。年三十九，以永興三年六月二十四日寢疾薨殂。背棄華殿，雲中名都。國失惠主，哀感欷歔。悲痛煩冤，載呼載號。遠近親軌，奔赴梓廬。仰訴造化，痛延悲夫！」時晉光熙元年也。

sourceRange.text: 長子衡，字伯玉，少以孝行著稱。學崔浩書，頗亦類焉。天安元年，擢爲內秘書中散。班下詔命及禦所覽書，多其跡也。衡舉李沖、李元愷、程駿等，終爲名器。承明元年，遷內都坐令，善折獄，孝文嘉之。太和二年，襲爵武陵公。衡涉獵書史，頗爲文筆。蠕蠕時犯塞，衡上書陳備禦之方、便國利人之策凡五十餘條。除秦州刺史，徙爵齊郡公。先是，河東年饑，劫盜大起。衡至，修龔遂法，勸課農桑，周年間，寇盜止息。卒，贈冀州刺史，諡惠公。衡五子。長子敞，字公世，襲爵，例降爲侯，爲平原相。

sourceRange.text: 長孫道生，嵩從子也。忠厚廉謹，道武愛其慎重，使掌機密。與賀毗等四人，內侍左右，出入詔命。明元即位，除南統將軍、冀州刺史。後取人美女以獻，明元切責之，以舊臣不加罪黜。太武即位，進爵汝陰公，遷廷尉卿。從征蠕蠕，與尉眷等率眾出白黑兩漠間，大捷而還。太武征赫連昌，道生與司徒長孫翰、宗正娥清為前驅，遂平其國。昌弟定走保平涼，宋遣將到彥之、王仲德寇河南以救定。詔道生與丹陽王太之屯河上以禦之。遂誘宋將檀道濟，邀其前後，追至曆城而還。除司空，加侍中，進封上党王。薨，年八十二，贈太尉，諡曰靖。

context.beforeSource: 晞曰：「莫尤我，我行事若不悔，久作三公矣。
context.afterSource: 皓字季高，少立名行，為士友所稱。

manualTranslations.zh: 齊亡，周武帝以晞為儀同大將軍、太子諫議大夫。
manualTranslations.literal: After Qi fell, Emperor Wu of Zhou made Xi Grand General with Equal Ceremonial and Grand Adviser to the Heir Apparent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Qi fell, Emperor Wu of Zhou made Xi Grand General with Equal Ceremonial and Grand Adviser to the Heir Apparent.

manualTranslations.zh: 隋開皇元年，卒於洛陽，年七十一。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Sui's Kaihuang era, he died at Luoyang at the age of seventy-one.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Sui's Kaihuang era, he died at Luoyang at seventy-one.

manualTranslations.zh: 贈儀同三司、曹州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: He was posthumously granted Commissioner with Protocol Equal to the Three Dukes and Inspector of Cao Province.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Commissioner with Protocol Equal to the Three Dukes and Inspector of Cao Province.

sourceRange.text: 太昌初，還洛。吏部尚書李神俊奏言：「比因多故，常侍遂無員限。今以王元景等為常侍，定限八員。」加金紫光祿大夫。武帝或時袒露，與近臣戲狎，每見昕，即正冠而斂容焉。昕體素甚肥，遭喪後，遂終身羸瘠。楊愔重其德素，以為人之師表。元象元年，兼散騎常侍，聘梁，魏收為副，並為朝廷所重。使還，高隆之求貨不得，諷憲台劾昕、收在江東大將商人市易，並坐禁止。齊文襄營救之。累遷秘書監。

context.beforeSource: 」邵乃免。
context.afterSource: 昕雅好清言，詞無淺俗。
context.beforeLocal: 邵乃免。
context.afterLocal: 昕雅好清言，詞無淺俗。

manualTranslations.zh: 太昌初，還洛。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he returned to Luoyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taichang, he returned to Luoyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 吏部尚書李神俊奏言：「比因多故，常侍遂無員限。
manualTranslations.literal: Minister of Personnel Li Shenjun memorialized, "Lately, because of many disturbances, the Regular Attendants have had no fixed quota.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Li Shenjun memorialized, "Lately, because of many disturbances, the Regular Attendants have had no fixed quota.

manualTranslations.zh: 今以王元景等為常侍，定限八員。」
manualTranslations.literal: Now, with Wang Yuanjing and the others as Regular Attendants, set the fixed limit at eight."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now, with Wang Yuanjing and the others as Regular Attendants, set the fixed limit at eight."

manualTranslations.zh: 加金紫光祿大夫。
manualTranslations.literal: He was additionally made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was additionally made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

manualTranslations.zh: 武帝或時袒露，與近臣戲狎，每見昕，即正冠而斂容焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Wu sometimes bared himself and joked familiarly with close ministers, but whenever he saw Xin, he straightened his cap and composed his expression.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu sometimes bared himself and joked familiarly with close ministers, but whenever he saw Xin, he straightened his cap and composed his expression.

manualTranslations.zh: 昕體素甚肥，遭喪後，遂終身羸瘠。
manualTranslations.literal: Xin had formerly been very stout, but after going through mourning he remained thin and wasted for the rest of his life.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xin had formerly been very stout, but after going through mourning he remained thin and wasted for the rest of his life.

manualTranslations.zh: 楊愔重其德素，以為人之師表。
manualTranslations.literal: Yang Yin esteemed his plain virtue and regarded him as a model for others.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yang Yin esteemed his plain virtue and regarded him as a model for others.

manualTranslations.zh: 元象元年，兼散騎常侍，聘梁，魏收為副，並為朝廷所重。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Yuanxiang, he concurrently served as Regular Attendant and went as envoy to Liang, with Wei Shou as his deputy; both were valued by the court.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanxiang, he concurrently served as Regular Attendant and went as envoy to Liang, with Wei Shou as his deputy; both were valued by the court.

manualTranslations.zh: 使還，高隆之求貨不得，諷憲台劾昕、收在江東大將商人市易，並坐禁止。
manualTranslations.literal: When the envoys returned, Gao Longzhi sought goods from them and did not get them, so he hinted to the censorate to impeach Xin and Shou for large-scale trading with merchants in Jiangdong; both were implicated and confined.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the envoys returned, Gao Longzhi sought goods from them and did not get them, so he hinted to the censorate to impeach Xin and Shou for large-scale trading with merchants in Jiangdong; both were implicated and confined.

manualTranslations.zh: 齊文襄營救之。
manualTranslations.literal: Wenxiang of Qi came to their rescue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wenxiang of Qi came to their rescue.

manualTranslations.zh: 累遷秘書監。
manualTranslations.literal: He rose through successive posts to Director of the Palace Library.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Director of the Palace Library.

sourceRange.text: 大寧元年，除衛尉少卿。尋兼散騎常侍，聘陳使主。行過彭城，讀道旁碑文未畢而絕倒。從者遙見，以為中惡。此碑乃贍父徐州時所立，故哀感焉。贍經熱病，面多瘢痕，然雍容可觀，辭韻溫雅，南人大相欽服。陳舍人劉師知見而心醉，乃言：「常侍，前朝通好之日何意不來？今日誰相對揚者！」其見重如此。還，襲爵武城公，再遷吏部郎中。因患耳，請急十餘日。舊式，百日不上，解官。吏部尚書尉瑾性偏急，以贍舉措舒緩，曹務煩劇，附驛奏聞。因見代，遂免歸。天統末，加驃騎大將軍，就拜銀青光祿大夫。卒，贈大理卿、濟州刺史，諡曰文。

context.beforeSource: 收慚遽，竟無一言。
context.afterSource: 贍性簡傲，以才地自矜，所與周旋，皆一時名望。
context.beforeLocal: 收慚遽，竟無一言。
context.afterLocal: 贍性簡傲，以才地自矜，所與周旋，皆一時名望。

manualTranslations.zh: 大寧元年，除衛尉少卿。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Daning, he was appointed Vice Chamberlain for the Palace Garrison.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daning, he was appointed Vice Chamberlain for the Palace Garrison.

manualTranslations.zh: 尋兼散騎常侍，聘陳使主。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon he concurrently served as Regular Attendant and was chief envoy on a mission to Chen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon he concurrently served as Regular Attendant and was chief envoy on a mission to Chen.

manualTranslations.zh: 行過彭城，讀道旁碑文未畢而絕倒。
manualTranslations.literal: As he passed Pengcheng, he was reading an inscription beside the road and collapsed before finishing it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As he passed Pengcheng, he was reading an inscription beside the road and collapsed before finishing it.

manualTranslations.zh: 從者遙見，以為中惡。
manualTranslations.literal: His attendants saw him from afar and thought he had been struck by a malign illness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His attendants saw him from afar and thought he had been struck by a malign illness.

manualTranslations.zh: 此碑乃贍父徐州時所立，故哀感焉。
manualTranslations.literal: The inscription had been erected when Zhan's father was in Xuzhou, and he was overcome with grief.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The inscription had been erected when Zhan's father was in Xuzhou, and he was overcome with grief.

manualTranslations.zh: 贍經熱病，面多瘢痕，然雍容可觀，辭韻溫雅，南人大相欽服。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhan had suffered a fever, and his face bore many scars, yet his bearing was graceful and impressive, his speech warm and elegant, and southerners greatly admired him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhan had suffered a fever, and his face bore many scars, yet his bearing was graceful and impressive, his speech warm and elegant, and southerners greatly admired him.

manualTranslations.zh: 陳舍人劉師知見而心醉，乃言：「常侍，前朝通好之日何意不來？
manualTranslations.literal: The Chen secretary Liu Shizhi saw him and was entranced, saying, "Regular Attendant, why did you not come in the days when the former dynasty maintained friendly relations?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Chen secretary Liu Shizhi saw him and was entranced, saying, "Regular Attendant, why did you not come in the days when the former dynasty maintained friendly relations?

manualTranslations.zh: 今日誰相對揚者！」
manualTranslations.literal: Who today could face you and answer you!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Who today could face you and answer you!"

manualTranslations.zh: 其見重如此。
manualTranslations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

manualTranslations.zh: 還，襲爵武城公，再遷吏部郎中。
manualTranslations.literal: After returning, he inherited the title Duke of Wucheng and was twice promoted, reaching Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After returning, he inherited the title Duke of Wucheng and was twice promoted, reaching Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.

manualTranslations.zh: 因患耳，請急十餘日。
manualTranslations.literal: Because of an ear ailment, he requested urgent leave for more than ten days.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because of an ear ailment, he requested urgent leave for more than ten days.

manualTranslations.zh: 舊式，百日不上，解官。
manualTranslations.literal: Under the old rule, if one did not report for duty for one hundred days, one was dismissed from office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under the old rule, if one did not report for duty for one hundred days, one was dismissed from office.

manualTranslations.zh: 吏部尚書尉瑾性偏急，以贍舉措舒緩，曹務煩劇，附驛奏聞。
manualTranslations.literal: Minister of Personnel Wei Jin was impatient by nature; because Zhan's conduct was unhurried while the ministry's business was urgent and heavy, he sent a memorial by courier.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Wei Jin was impatient by nature; because Zhan's conduct was unhurried while the ministry's business was urgent and heavy, he sent a memorial by courier.

manualTranslations.zh: 因見代，遂免歸。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhan was therefore replaced, dismissed, and sent home.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhan was therefore replaced, dismissed, and sent home.

manualTranslations.zh: 天統末，加驃騎大將軍，就拜銀青光祿大夫。
manualTranslations.literal: At the end of Tiantong, he was additionally made General of Agile Cavalry and then appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the end of Tiantong, he was additionally made General of Agile Cavalry and then appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.

manualTranslations.zh: 卒，贈大理卿、濟州刺史，諡曰文。
manualTranslations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously granted Chamberlain for Judicial Review and Inspector of Ji Province, with the posthumous name Wen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously granted Chamberlain for Judicial Review and Inspector of Ji Province, with the posthumous name Wen.

localRange.text: 父放，慕容痈吏部尚書。

manualTranslations.zh: 父放，慕容暐吏部尚書。
manualTranslations.literal: His father Fang was Minister of Personnel under Murong Wei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His father Fang was Minister of Personnel under Murong Wei.

samePatternLocalRepairs: 仕慕容暐，補著作郎，撰《燕記》。
回字叔念，孝文賜名焉，慕容暐太尉奕之後也。

sourceRange.text: 王憲，字顯則，北海劇人也。其先姓田，秦始皇滅齊，田氏稱王家子孫，因以為氏。仍居海岱。祖猛，仕苻堅，位丞相。父休，河東太守。憲幼孤，隨伯父永在鄴。苻丕稱尊號，復以永為丞相。永為慕容永所殺，憲匿於清河人家。皇始中，乃歸魏。道武見之，曰：「此王猛孫也。」厚禮待之，以為本州中正，領選曹事，兼掌門下。太武即位，遷廷尉卿。出為上谷太守，賜爵高唐子。清身率下，風化大行。尋拜外都大官，復移中都。歷任二曹，斷獄稱旨。進爵劇縣侯。出為并州刺史，又進北海公。境內清肅。及還京師。以憲年老，特賜錦繡布帛，珍羞醴膳。天安初，卒，年八十九。諡曰康。子崇襲。

context.beforeSource: 及魏克青州，懷順迎邪利喪還青州云。
context.afterSource: 崇弟嶷，字道長。
context.beforeLocal: 及魏克青州，懷順迎邪利喪還青州云。
context.afterLocal: 崇弟嶷，字道長。

manualTranslations.zh: 王憲，字顯則，北海劇人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Wang Xian, styled Xianze, was from Ju in Beihai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Xian, styled Xianze, was from Ju in Beihai.

manualTranslations.zh: 其先姓田，秦始皇滅齊，田氏稱王家子孫，因以為氏。
manualTranslations.literal: His ancestors had been surnamed Tian. When the First Emperor of Qin destroyed Qi, the Tian clan called themselves descendants of the royal house and therefore took Wang as their surname.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His ancestors had been surnamed Tian. When the First Emperor of Qin destroyed Qi, the Tian clan called themselves descendants of the royal house and therefore took Wang as their surname.

manualTranslations.zh: 仍居海岱。
manualTranslations.literal: They continued to live in the Haidai region.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They continued to live in the Haidai region.

manualTranslations.zh: 祖猛，仕苻堅，位丞相。
manualTranslations.literal: His grandfather Meng served Fu Jian and held the post of Chancellor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His grandfather Meng served Fu Jian and held the post of Chancellor.

manualTranslations.zh: 父休，河東太守。
manualTranslations.literal: His father Xiu was Administrator of Hedong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His father Xiu was Administrator of Hedong.

manualTranslations.zh: 憲幼孤，隨伯父永在鄴。
manualTranslations.literal: Xian was orphaned young and followed his uncle Yong to Ye.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xian was orphaned young and followed his uncle Yong to Ye.

manualTranslations.zh: 苻丕稱尊號，復以永為丞相。
manualTranslations.literal: When Fu Pi assumed the imperial title, he again made Yong Chancellor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Fu Pi assumed the imperial title, he again made Yong Chancellor.

manualTranslations.zh: 永為慕容永所殺，憲匿於清河人家。
manualTranslations.literal: Yong was killed by Murong Yong, and Xian hid in the home of a man from Qinghe.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yong was killed by Murong Yong, and Xian hid in the home of a man from Qinghe.

manualTranslations.zh: 皇始中，乃歸魏。
manualTranslations.literal: During the Huangshi era, he returned to Wei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During the Huangshi era, he returned to Wei.

manualTranslations.zh: 道武見之，曰：「此王猛孫也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Daowu saw him and said, "This is Wang Meng's grandson."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Daowu saw him and said, "This is Wang Meng's grandson."

manualTranslations.zh: 厚禮待之，以為本州中正，領選曹事，兼掌門下。
manualTranslations.literal: He treated him with generous courtesy, made him Rectifier for his home province, put him in charge of selection affairs, and also had him serve in the Chancellery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He treated him with generous courtesy, made him Rectifier for his home province, put him in charge of selection affairs, and also had him serve in the Chancellery.

manualTranslations.zh: 太武即位，遷廷尉卿。
manualTranslations.literal: When Taiwu took the throne, Xian was transferred to Chamberlain for Law Enforcement.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Taiwu took the throne, Xian was transferred to Chamberlain for Law Enforcement.

manualTranslations.zh: 出為上谷太守，賜爵高唐子。
manualTranslations.literal: He was sent out as Administrator of Shanggu and granted the title Viscount of Gaotang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Administrator of Shanggu and granted the title Viscount of Gaotang.

manualTranslations.zh: 清身率下，風化大行。
manualTranslations.literal: He kept himself pure and led his subordinates by example, and moral transformation spread widely.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He kept himself pure and led his subordinates by example, and moral transformation spread widely.

manualTranslations.zh: 尋拜外都大官，復移中都。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon he was appointed Outer Capital High Official and was later moved to the Central Capital.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Outer Capital High Official and was later moved to the Central Capital.

manualTranslations.zh: 歷任二曹，斷獄稱旨。
manualTranslations.literal: He served successively in two departments, and his adjudication of cases accorded with the emperor's wishes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He served successively in two departments, and his adjudication of cases accorded with the emperor's wishes.

manualTranslations.zh: 進爵劇縣侯。
manualTranslations.literal: His title was advanced to Marquis of Ju County.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His title was advanced to Marquis of Ju County.

manualTranslations.zh: 出為并州刺史，又進北海公。
manualTranslations.literal: He was sent out as Inspector of Bing Province and was further advanced to Duke of Beihai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Inspector of Bing Province and was further advanced to Duke of Beihai.

manualTranslations.zh: 境內清肅。
manualTranslations.literal: Within his territory all was clean and orderly.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Within his territory all was clean and orderly.

manualTranslations.zh: 及還京師。
manualTranslations.literal: When he returned to the capital,
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he returned to the capital,

manualTranslations.zh: 以憲年老，特賜錦繡布帛，珍羞醴膳。
manualTranslations.literal: because Xian was old, he was specially given brocade, embroidered cloth, silk, delicacies, sweet wine, and fine meals.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: because Xian was old, he was specially given brocade, embroidered cloth, silk, delicacies, sweet wine, and fine meals.

manualTranslations.zh: 天安初，卒，年八十九。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of Tian'an, he died at eighty-nine.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tian'an, he died at eighty-nine.

manualTranslations.zh: 諡曰康。
manualTranslations.literal: His posthumous name was Kang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Kang.

manualTranslations.zh: 子崇襲。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Chong inherited.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Chong inherited.

manualTranslations.zh: 乾歸有氣幹，頗習書疏，尤好兵法。
manualTranslations.literal: Qiangui had vigor and ability, was fairly practiced in documents and memorials, and especially liked military methods.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Qiangui had vigor and ability, was fairly practiced in documents and memorials, and especially liked military methods.

manualTranslations.zh: 尚景穆女安樂公主，除駙馬都尉、侍中。
manualTranslations.literal: He married Jingmu’s daughter, Princess Anle, and was appointed Commandant Escort and Palace Attendant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He married Jingmu’s daughter, Princess Anle, and was appointed Commandant Escort and Palace Attendant.

manualTranslations.zh: 獻文初，為秦州刺史，有惠政。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of Xianwen’s reign, he became Inspector of Qin Province and governed benevolently.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianwen’s reign, he became Inspector of Qin Province and governed benevolently.

manualTranslations.zh: 孝文即位，為中道都將。
manualTranslations.literal: When Xiaowen took the throne, he became Chief Commander of the Central Route.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Xiaowen took the throne, he became Chief Commander of the Central Route.

manualTranslations.zh: 卒，諡曰康。
manualTranslations.literal: He died and received the posthumous name Kang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died and received the posthumous name Kang.

manualTranslations.zh: 子海，字懷仁，位散騎侍郎。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Hai, styled Huairen, held the post of Gentleman Cavalier Attendant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Hai, styled Huairen, held the post of Gentleman Cavalier Attendant.

manualTranslations.zh: 卒，諡曰孝。
manualTranslations.literal: He died and received the posthumous name Xiao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died and received the posthumous name Xiao.

sourceRange.text: 王洛兒，京兆人也。明元在東宮，以善騎射給事帳下，謹願未嘗有過。明元嘗獵于灅南，冰陷沒馬。洛兒投水奉帝出，殆將凍死。帝解衣賜之，自是恩寵日隆。天賜末，帝避難居外，洛兒晨夜侍衛，恭勤發于至誠。元紹之逆，帝左右唯洛兒與車路頭。晝居山嶺，夜還洛兒家。洛兒鄰人李道潛相奉給，晨復還山。眾庶頗知，喜而相告。紹聞，收道斬之。洛兒猶冒難往返京都，通問于大臣，大臣遂出奉迎，百姓奔赴。明元還宮，社稷獲全，洛兒有功焉。明元即位，拜散騎常侍，賜爵新息公，加直意將軍。又追贈其父為列侯，賜僮隸五十戶。卒。贈太尉、建平王。賜溫明秘器，載以巉輬車，使殿中衛士為之導從，親臨哀慟者四焉。乃鴆其妻周氏，與合葬。子長城襲爵。

context.beforeSource: 子歇襲爵。
context.afterSource: 車路頭，代人也。

items.notes: Restored the omitted biography of Wang Luo’er.

manualTranslations.zh: 王洛兒，京兆人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Wang Luo’er was a man of Jingzhao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Luo’er was a man of Jingzhao.

manualTranslations.zh: 明元在東宮，以善騎射給事帳下，謹願未嘗有過。
manualTranslations.literal: When Mingyuan was in the Eastern Palace, Wang served in his retinue because he was skilled at mounted archery; he was careful and sincere and never committed an offense.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Mingyuan was in the Eastern Palace, Wang served in his retinue because he was skilled at mounted archery; he was careful and sincere and never committed an offense.

manualTranslations.zh: 明元嘗獵于灅南，冰陷沒馬。
manualTranslations.literal: Mingyuan once hunted south of the Lei, where the ice gave way and swallowed his horse.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mingyuan once hunted south of the Lei, where the ice gave way and swallowed his horse.

manualTranslations.zh: 洛兒投水奉帝出，殆將凍死。
manualTranslations.literal: Luo’er plunged into the water and brought the emperor out, nearly freezing to death.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Luo’er plunged into the water and brought the emperor out, nearly freezing to death.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝解衣賜之，自是恩寵日隆。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor took off his own garment and bestowed it on him, and from then on his favor and honor increased daily.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor took off his own garment and bestowed it on him, and from then on his favor and honor increased daily.

manualTranslations.zh: 天賜末，帝避難居外，洛兒晨夜侍衛，恭勤發于至誠。
manualTranslations.literal: At the end of the Tianci era, when the emperor took refuge outside the palace, Luo’er guarded and attended him day and night, his reverent diligence coming from complete sincerity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianci era, when the emperor took refuge outside the palace, Luo’er guarded and attended him day and night, his reverent diligence coming from complete sincerity.

manualTranslations.zh: 元紹之逆，帝左右唯洛兒與車路頭。
manualTranslations.literal: During Yuan Shao’s rebellion, only Luo’er and Che Lutou remained at the emperor’s side.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During Yuan Shao’s rebellion, only Luo’er and Che Lutou remained at the emperor’s side.

manualTranslations.zh: 晝居山嶺，夜還洛兒家。
manualTranslations.literal: By day the emperor stayed in the hills, and at night he returned to Luo’er’s house.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By day the emperor stayed in the hills, and at night he returned to Luo’er’s house.

manualTranslations.zh: 洛兒鄰人李道潛相奉給，晨復還山。
manualTranslations.literal: Luo’er’s neighbor Li Daoqian supplied them, and in the morning they returned to the mountains.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Luo’er’s neighbor Li Daoqian supplied them, and in the morning they returned to the mountains.

manualTranslations.zh: 眾庶頗知，喜而相告。
manualTranslations.literal: Many common people came to know of it, rejoiced, and told one another.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Many common people came to know of it, rejoiced, and told one another.

manualTranslations.zh: 紹聞，收道斬之。
manualTranslations.literal: When Shao heard of it, he arrested Daoqian and had him beheaded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Shao heard of it, he arrested Daoqian and had him beheaded.

manualTranslations.zh: 洛兒猶冒難往返京都，通問于大臣，大臣遂出奉迎，百姓奔赴。
manualTranslations.literal: Luo’er still braved danger to travel back and forth to the capital, communicating with the great ministers; the ministers then came out to receive the emperor, and the people rushed to him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Luo’er still braved danger to travel back and forth to the capital, communicating with the great ministers; the ministers then came out to receive the emperor, and the people rushed to him.

manualTranslations.zh: 明元還宮，社稷獲全，洛兒有功焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Mingyuan returned to the palace, the state was preserved, and Luo’er had merit in it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mingyuan returned to the palace, the state was preserved, and Luo’er had merit in it.

manualTranslations.zh: 明元即位，拜散騎常侍，賜爵新息公，加直意將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: When Mingyuan took the throne, Luo’er was appointed Cavalier Regular Attendant, granted the title Duke of Xinxi, and additionally made General of Direct Intention.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Mingyuan took the throne, Luo’er was appointed Cavalier Regular Attendant, granted the title Duke of Xinxi, and additionally made General of Direct Intention.

manualTranslations.zh: 又追贈其父為列侯，賜僮隸五十戶。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor also posthumously made his father a ranked marquis and granted him fifty households of servants.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor also posthumously made his father a ranked marquis and granted him fifty households of servants.

manualTranslations.zh: 卒。
manualTranslations.literal: He died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died.

manualTranslations.zh: 贈太尉、建平王。
manualTranslations.literal: He was posthumously granted the offices of Grand Commandant and Prince of Jianping.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the offices of Grand Commandant and Prince of Jianping.

manualTranslations.zh: 賜溫明秘器，載以巉輬車，使殿中衛士為之導從，親臨哀慟者四焉。
manualTranslations.literal: He was granted the Wenming burial coffer and carried on a chanliang carriage; palace guards were made to escort the procession, and the emperor personally came to mourn him four times.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was granted the Wenming burial coffer and carried on a chanliang carriage; palace guards were made to escort the procession, and the emperor personally came to mourn him four times.

manualTranslations.zh: 乃鴆其妻周氏，與合葬。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon his wife, Lady Zhou, was poisoned and buried with him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thereupon his wife, Lady Zhou, was poisoned and buried with him.

manualTranslations.zh: 子長城襲爵。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Changcheng inherited the title.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Changcheng inherited the title.

sourceRange.text: 和其奴，代人也。少有操行，善射禦。初為三郎。文成初，封平昌公，累遷尚書左僕射。又與河東王閭毗、太宰常英等並平尚書事。在官慎法，不受私請。遷司空，加侍中。文成崩，乙渾與林金閭擅殺尚書楊保年等。時殿中尚書元郁率殿中宿衛士欲加兵於渾。渾懼，歸咎于金閭，執以付鬱。時其奴以金閭罪惡未分，出之為定州刺史。皇興元年，長安鎮將東平王道符反，詔其奴討之，未至而道符敗。軍還，薨，內外嘆惜之。贈平昌王，諡曰宣。子受襲爵。苟頹，代人也。本姓若干。父洛拔，內行長。頹厚重寡言，少嚴毅清直，武力過人。擢為中散，小心謹敬。太武至江，賜爵建德男。累遷司衛監、洛州刺史。抑強扶弱，山蠻畏威，不敢為寇。太和中，歷位侍中、都曹尚書，進爵河南公。頹方正好直言，雖文明太后生殺不允，頹亦言至懇切。李惠、李䐶之誅，頹並致諫。遷司空，進爵河東王。以舊老，聽乘步挽，杖於朝。大駕行幸三川，頹留守京師。沙門法秀謀反，頹率禁旅收掩畢獲，內外晏然。薨，諡僖王。長子愷襲爵河東王，例降為公。

manualTranslations.zh: 和其奴，代人也。
manualTranslations.literal: He Qinu was a man of Dai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He Qinu was a man of Dai.

manualTranslations.zh: 少有操行，善射禦。
manualTranslations.literal: In youth he had moral conduct and was good at archery and driving.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In youth he had moral conduct and was good at archery and driving.

manualTranslations.zh: 初為三郎。
manualTranslations.literal: At first he served as Gentleman of the Third Rank.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At first he served as Gentleman of the Third Rank.

manualTranslations.zh: 文成初，封平昌公，累遷尚書左僕射。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of Wencheng’s reign, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingchang and was repeatedly promoted, becoming Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wencheng’s reign, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingchang and was repeatedly promoted, becoming Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

manualTranslations.zh: 又與河東王閭毗、太宰常英等並平尚書事。
manualTranslations.literal: He also managed the affairs of the Masters of Writing together with Prince Lu Pi of Hedong, Grand Preceptor Chang Ying, and the others.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also managed the affairs of the Masters of Writing together with Prince Lu Pi of Hedong, Grand Preceptor Chang Ying, and the others.

manualTranslations.zh: 在官慎法，不受私請。
manualTranslations.literal: In office he was careful with the law and did not accept private requests.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In office he was careful with the law and did not accept private requests.

manualTranslations.zh: 遷司空，加侍中。
manualTranslations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Works and additionally made Palace Attendant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Works and additionally made Palace Attendant.

manualTranslations.zh: 文成崩，乙渾與林金閭擅殺尚書楊保年等。
manualTranslations.literal: When Wencheng died, Yihun and Lin Jinlü arbitrarily killed Minister Yang Baonian and others.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Wencheng died, Yihun and Lin Jinlü arbitrarily killed Minister Yang Baonian and others.

manualTranslations.zh: 時殿中尚書元郁率殿中宿衛士欲加兵於渾。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time, Palace Minister Yuan Yu led the palace night guards and intended to attack Hun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the time, Palace Minister Yuan Yu led the palace night guards and intended to attack Hun.

manualTranslations.zh: 渾懼，歸咎于金閭，執以付鬱。
manualTranslations.literal: Hun became afraid, shifted the blame to Jinlü, arrested him, and handed him over to Yu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hun became afraid, shifted the blame to Jinlü, arrested him, and handed him over to Yu.

manualTranslations.zh: 時其奴以金閭罪惡未分，出之為定州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time, Qinu considered Jinlü’s guilt not yet clearly determined and sent him out as Inspector of Ding Province.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the time, Qinu considered Jinlü’s guilt not yet clearly determined and sent him out as Inspector of Ding Province.

manualTranslations.zh: 皇興元年，長安鎮將東平王道符反，詔其奴討之，未至而道符敗。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Huangxing, Daofu, Prince of Dongping and Garrison Commander of Chang’an, rebelled; an edict ordered Qinu to attack him, but before Qinu arrived Daofu was defeated.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangxing, Daofu, Prince of Dongping and Garrison Commander of Chang’an, rebelled; an edict ordered Qinu to attack him, but before Qinu arrived Daofu was defeated.

manualTranslations.zh: 軍還，薨，內外嘆惜之。
manualTranslations.literal: When the army returned, Qinu died, and those inside and outside the court lamented him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Qinu died, and those inside and outside the court lamented him.

manualTranslations.zh: 贈平昌王，諡曰宣。
manualTranslations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Prince of Pingchang, with the posthumous name Xuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Prince of Pingchang, with the posthumous name Xuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 子受襲爵。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Shou inherited the title.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Shou inherited the title.

manualTranslations.zh: 苟頹，代人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Gou Tui was a man of Dai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gou Tui was a man of Dai.

manualTranslations.zh: 本姓若干。
manualTranslations.literal: His original surname was Ruogan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His original surname was Ruogan.

manualTranslations.zh: 父洛拔，內行長。
manualTranslations.literal: His father Luoba was Chief of Inner Conduct.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His father Luoba was Chief of Inner Conduct.

manualTranslations.zh: 頹厚重寡言，少嚴毅清直，武力過人。
manualTranslations.literal: Tui was steady and taciturn; from youth he was stern, resolute, pure, and upright, with physical strength surpassing others.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tui was steady and taciturn; from youth he was stern, resolute, pure, and upright, with physical strength surpassing others.

manualTranslations.zh: 擢為中散，小心謹敬。
manualTranslations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Cadet and was careful, cautious, and respectful.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Cadet and was careful, cautious, and respectful.

manualTranslations.zh: 太武至江，賜爵建德男。
manualTranslations.literal: When Taiwu reached the Yangtze, Tui was granted the title Baron of Jiande.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Taiwu reached the Yangtze, Tui was granted the title Baron of Jiande.

manualTranslations.zh: 累遷司衛監、洛州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted, becoming Director of Palace Security and Inspector of Luo Province.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted, becoming Director of Palace Security and Inspector of Luo Province.

manualTranslations.zh: 抑強扶弱，山蠻畏威，不敢為寇。
manualTranslations.literal: He restrained the strong and supported the weak; the mountain Man feared his authority and did not dare to raid.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He restrained the strong and supported the weak; the mountain Man feared his authority and did not dare to raid.

manualTranslations.zh: 太和中，歷位侍中、都曹尚書，進爵河南公。
manualTranslations.literal: During the Taihe era, he successively held the posts of Palace Attendant and Minister of the Bureau of All Offices, and was advanced to Duke of Henan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era, he successively held the posts of Palace Attendant and Minister of the Bureau of All Offices, and was advanced to Duke of Henan.

manualTranslations.zh: 頹方正好直言，雖文明太后生殺不允，頹亦言至懇切。
manualTranslations.literal: Tui was upright and liked to speak frankly; even when Empress Dowager Wenming’s decisions of life and death were unjust, Tui spoke with utmost earnestness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tui was upright and liked to speak frankly; even when Empress Dowager Wenming’s decisions of life and death were unjust, Tui spoke with utmost earnestness.

manualTranslations.zh: 李惠、李䐶之誅，頹並致諫。
manualTranslations.literal: At the executions of Li Hui and Li Xin, Tui remonstrated in both cases.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the executions of Li Hui and Li Xin, Tui remonstrated in both cases.

manualTranslations.zh: 遷司空，進爵河東王。
manualTranslations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Works and advanced to Prince of Hedong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Works and advanced to Prince of Hedong.

manualTranslations.zh: 以舊老，聽乘步挽，杖於朝。
manualTranslations.literal: Because he was an old minister, he was permitted to ride a hand-drawn carriage and use a staff at court.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because he was an old minister, he was permitted to ride a hand-drawn carriage and use a staff at court.

manualTranslations.zh: 大駕行幸三川，頹留守京師。
manualTranslations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Sanchuan, Tui remained behind to guard the capital.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage visited Sanchuan, Tui remained behind to guard the capital.

manualTranslations.zh: 沙門法秀謀反，頹率禁旅收掩畢獲，內外晏然。
manualTranslations.literal: When the monk Faxiu plotted rebellion, Tui led the palace troops to arrest and seize the conspirators, capturing them all, and the court and capital were calm.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the monk Faxiu plotted rebellion, Tui led the palace troops to arrest and seize the conspirators, capturing them all, and the court and capital were calm.

manualTranslations.zh: 薨，諡僖王。
manualTranslations.literal: He died and received the posthumous title Prince Xi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died and received the posthumous title Prince Xi.

manualTranslations.zh: 長子愷襲爵河東王，例降為公。
manualTranslations.literal: His eldest son Kai inherited the title Prince of Hedong, which by regulation was reduced to duke.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His eldest son Kai inherited the title Prince of Hedong, which by regulation was reduced to duke.

sourceRange.text: 周幾，代人也。少以善射為獵郎。明元即位，為左部尚書，以軍功封交趾侯。太武以幾有智勇，遣鎮河南，威信著於外境。幾常嫌奚斤等綏撫關中失和，每至言論，形於聲色，斤等憚焉。進號宋兵將軍，率洛州刺史于栗磾以萬人襲陝城，卒于軍，軍人無不嘆惜之。歸葬京師。諡曰桓。子步襲爵。

localRange.text: 周幾，代人也。少以善射為獵郎。明元即位，為左部尚書，以軍功封交趾侯。太武以幾有智勇，遣鎮河南，威信著於外境。幾常嫌奚斤等綏撫關中失和，每至言論，形於聲色，斤等憚焉。進號宋兵將軍，率洛州刺史于栗磾以萬人襲陝城，卒于軍，軍人無不嘆惜之。歸葬京師。諡曰桓。子步襲爵。

context.beforeSource: 天平元年，舉兵應樊子鵠，戰敗死。
context.afterSource: 豆代田，代人也。

manualTranslations.zh: 周幾，代人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhou Ji was a man of Dai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhou Ji was a man of Dai.

manualTranslations.zh: 少以善射為獵郎。
manualTranslations.literal: In youth, because he was good at archery, he became a hunting gentleman.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In youth, because he was good at archery, he became a hunting gentleman.

manualTranslations.zh: 明元即位，為左部尚書，以軍功封交趾侯。
manualTranslations.literal: When Mingyuan took the throne, he became Minister of the Left Section and, for military merit, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiaozhi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Mingyuan took the throne, he became Minister of the Left Section and, for military merit, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiaozhi.

manualTranslations.zh: 太武以幾有智勇，遣鎮河南，威信著於外境。
manualTranslations.literal: Taiwu considered Ji wise and brave and sent him to garrison Henan, where his authority and trustworthiness were known beyond the frontier.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taiwu considered Ji wise and brave and sent him to garrison Henan, where his authority and trustworthiness were known beyond the frontier.

manualTranslations.zh: 幾常嫌奚斤等綏撫關中失和，每至言論，形於聲色，斤等憚焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Ji often disapproved that Xi Jin and the others had lost harmony in pacifying Guanzhong; whenever the matter came up, it showed in his voice and expression, and Jin and the others feared him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ji often disapproved that Xi Jin and the others had lost harmony in pacifying Guanzhong; whenever the matter came up, it showed in his voice and expression, and Jin and the others feared him.

manualTranslations.zh: 進號宋兵將軍，率洛州刺史于栗磾以萬人襲陝城，卒于軍，軍人無不嘆惜之。
manualTranslations.literal: He was advanced in title to General of Song Troops and led Inspector Yu Lidi of Luo Province and ten thousand men in a surprise attack on Shaan City. He died in the army, and none of the soldiers failed to lament him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was advanced in title to General of Song Troops and led Inspector Yu Lidi of Luo Province and ten thousand men in a surprise attack on Shaan City. He died in the army, and none of the soldiers failed to lament him.

manualTranslations.zh: 歸葬京師。
manualTranslations.literal: He was returned for burial in the capital.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was returned for burial in the capital.

manualTranslations.zh: 諡曰桓。
manualTranslations.literal: His posthumous name was Huan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Huan.

manualTranslations.zh: 子步襲爵。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Bu inherited the title.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Bu inherited the title.

sourceRange.text: 與万俟醜奴戰，沒。

localRange.text: 與万俟晗鬼奴戰，沒。

context.beforeSource: 累遷直寢。
context.afterSource: 論曰：古弼軍謀經國，有柱石之量；

context.afterLocal: 論曰：古弼軍謀經國，有柱石之量；

manualTranslations.zh: 與万俟醜奴戰，沒。
manualTranslations.literal: Fighting Moqi Chounu, he was killed in battle.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He fell in battle against Moqi Chounu.

sourceRange.text: 尉撥，代人也。父那，濮陽太守。撥為太學生，募從兗州刺史羅忸擊賊于陳、汝，有功，賜爵介休男。討和龍，擊吐谷渾，皆有軍功，進爵為子。累遷杏城鎮將，大得人和。文成以撥清平有惠績，賜以衣服。獻文即位，為北征都將。南攻懸瓠。進爵安城侯，位北豫州刺史。卒，諡敬侯。陸真，代人也。父洛侯，秦州刺史。真少善騎射。太武以真膂力過人，拜內三郎。真君中，從討蠕蠕，以功賜爵關內侯。後攻懸瓠，登樓臨射城中，弦不虛發。從太武至江，還攻盱眙，真功居多。文成即位，進爵都昌侯，位選部尚書。後拜長安平鎮將。時初置長蛇鎮，真率眾築城未訖，而氐豪仇傉檀等反叛。真擊平之，卒城長蛇而還。東平王道符反于長安，以真為長安鎮將，賜爵河南公。長安平兵人素伏其威信，及至，皆怗然安靜。在鎮數年，甚著威稱。卒，諡曰烈。

context.beforeSource: 帝怒，絕其爵云。
context.afterSource: 子延，字契胡提，頗有氣幹。
